title: Learner groups in courses: ideas from other products
intro: This page gathers ideas for putting learners into groups inside a course in Essentials 2.0. Screens from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero show how products handle existing groups. They cover inheriting members, reviewing who will be enrolled, showing a roster, bulk entry, limits and notification choices. Some examples come from courses; others are nearby patterns from projects, events or bookings. None of the examples shows a group that stays in sync with a learning management system (LMS). We kept 21 examples across 12 products instead of adding weaker ones to reach a larger number.

questions.title: When you attach a group, does membership stay in sync, or is it a one-time copy?
questions.answer: Treat picking a group as separate from keeping its membership in sync later. Circle lets you inherit members from an existing space group when you create a course space. Asana lets you add teams when setting access on a project template. Neither example shows that later group changes keep flowing into the course. Basecamp states the opposite: later group changes do not update earlier assignments or mentions. For Essentials, spell out the membership rule you choose; whether to sync later still needs a product decision.

questions.title: How do products preview the impact before you confirm (counts, conflicts, already enrolled)?
questions.answer: Put the affected count next to the action. Deel shows 'Selected 96 of 96 items' and a whole-team warning. Gusto reviews the learner count, completion date, reminders and cost, with 'Edit' links. GitBook puts the count in an 'Add 1 member' action. These support count-based review, but none shows how duplicates, already enrolled learners or newly added learners are handled. Those remain requirements to check when semester groups overlap.

questions.title: What does the roster show: status, role, group origin and exceptions?
questions.answer: Treat role, enrollment status, activity and group origin as different kinds of information. One Circle members table shows role and activity. Another Circle course view emphasizes progress and start dates. Teachable filters students by course and offers bulk actions. None shows labels for where access came from, or per-learner sync exceptions. Essentials still needs a decision on how a roster explains why each learner has access.

questions.title: How do bulk paths (CSV, link or integration) sit beside manual add?
questions.answer: Keep other entry paths next to the manual action. Teachable shows manual enrollment beside an 'Import CSV' tab, with a course target and success feedback on the manual path. Partiful is a nearby event pattern with a CSV template and a review of recipients. Circle also offers CSV and link paths when inviting members. These are visible entry points; none of the kept flows proves LMS integration, CSV conflict handling or ongoing roster sync.

questions.title: How do products handle capacity, waitlists and enrollment windows?
questions.answer: Separate a course limit from what happens when the course is full. Podia shows course start date and sign-up limit settings. Luma pairs event capacity with an optional waitlist. Fresha collects date and time preferences when someone joins a booking waitlist. The event and booking patterns are nearby ideas, not direct course enrollment. Deel adds immediate or scheduled assignment and an optional deadline; Gusto adds completion reminders and still allows overdue completion. Those are assignment or completion dates, not enrollment cutoffs. No example settles an oversize group, partial admission, closing dates or waitlist promotion.

questions.title: How do products notify learners on enrollment (hand-off to modules 07 and 09)?
questions.answer: Show the notification choice at enrollment confirmation. Circle separates 'Send invites' from 'Add without notification'. Gusto explains future course emails and learner next steps before purchase; that is a disclosure, not proof an email was sent. Cloudflare shows what not to copy: a restricted 'Skip confirmation email' option that fails the invitation. These screens show controls and failure feedback, not actual email delivery. Keep the course-side choice and outcome here; learner-facing access and message content stay in modules 07 and 09.

references.title: Select people or teams for a project template
references.question: Q1
references.take: Asana's project-template member field accepts people or teams. It says private teams are added only when the project creator is a member. No existing team is selected on this screen, and completed attachment or ongoing sync is not shown.

references.title: Group policy that copies members once
references.question: Q1
references.take: Basecamp explains that choosing a group expands its current members. Later membership changes do not update previous assignments or mentions. This is an explicit one-time copy, not live course-group sync.

references.title: Inherit members from a course space group
references.question: Q1
references.take: When creating a course space, Circle lets you select a Space group and optionally 'Add members from this space group'. Inheritance from an existing group is visible. The screenshots do not show whether later membership changes keep flowing in.

references.title: Review workers before assigning a course
references.question: Q2
references.take: Deel's 'Assign workers to course' screen shows 'Selected 96 of 96 items', worker details, a whole-team warning and 'Continue' into 'Schedule Assignment'. It does not show duplicate learners or how many learners are new to the course.

references.title: Review eligible workers before selection
references.question: Q2
references.take: Deel shows 'Total 96 items', worker details and group, status and type filters. 'Continue' stays disabled until someone is selected. A whole-team access warning says missing workers may need Engage access updated. This is not a selected-learner count or duplicate-conflict screen.

references.title: Show the selected count before adding
references.question: Q2
references.take: GitBook's searchable, role-filtered member picker shows '1 selected' and 'Add 1 member'. This is a team-access analogy for putting a count on the enrollment confirmation.

references.title: Review training count, dates and reminders
references.question: Q2
references.take: Before purchase, Gusto's 'Review' screen shows the course name, number of team members, completion due date and reminder timing, with 'Edit' links. This is a pre-commit review, not proof enrollment finished or a notification was sent.

references.title: Review a training assignment before purchase
references.question: Q2
references.take: Gusto lets you select a member, set a due date and an optional seven-day email reminder. Then you review course, count, date and reminders with 'Edit' links. It also shows per-person and total cost plus a post-purchase email note. The captured flow stops before purchase, so it does not prove enrollment or email delivery.

references.title: Member roles and activity in a roster
references.question: Q3
references.take: Circle's Members table shows role, joined date, paywall and last activity, with add and export controls. It does not show where access came from or individual enrollment exceptions.

references.title: Course student progress beside activity
references.question: Q3
references.take: Circle's course dashboard shows student progress, last activity and start date; later screens visit comments. Course status 'Open' is not a learner enrollment status. Roles, group origin and exceptions are not shown.

references.title: Filter students by course enrollment
references.question: Q3
references.take: Teachable's Students table filters by 'Enrolled In Specific Course(s)' and offers bulk actions, email opt-out and account or activity details. It is filtered by course; group origin and exceptions are not shown.

references.title: CSV invite preparation with a review area
references.question: Q4
references.take: Partiful's event invite screen puts 'Add Manually' and 'Bulk Add', a CSV template with Name and Email headers, recipient review, a message and 'Send emails' in one place. This does not prove course enrollment or delivery.

references.title: Manual enrollment beside CSV import
references.question: Q4
references.take: Teachable walks from Students to 'Add Students', manual entry, choosing a course or product and payment or access basis, then 'Import' with success feedback. 'Import CSV' is a sibling tab, but its mapping and run are not captured.

references.title: Schedule assignment and optional deadline
references.question: Q5
references.take: After selecting workers, Deel lets you choose immediate or scheduled assignment, optionally set a deadline, then 'Assign (96)'. This is assignment timing and a completion deadline, not an enrollment open or closing window.

references.title: Collect preferences on a booking waitlist
references.question: Q5
references.take: In Fresha, a full date leads to date and time preferences, a first-visit question, payment and notes review, then 'Join the waitlist'. It does not establish course-level capacity, queue priority or automatic promotion.

references.title: Set completion dates and automatic reminders
references.question: Q5
references.take: Gusto's training assignment separates participant selection, dates and reminders, then review. Settings include a completion due date, reminders near the deadline, a seven-day reminder toggle and an email preview. Overdue completion remains possible. A due date is not an enrollment cutoff.

references.title: Pair event capacity with a waitlist
references.question: Q5
references.take: Luma's 'Max Capacity' setting says registration closes at the limit and offers an 'Over-Capacity Waitlist' toggle. Rules for admitting or promoting a whole group are not shown.

references.title: Set course start date and sign-up limit
references.question: Q5
references.take: Podia's Course Availability groups 'Start date' and 'Sign-up limit' under Limits, with no-limit and limited-sign-up options. Enrollment closing dates and attaching an oversize group are not shown.

references.title: Choose invitation email or silent addition
references.question: Q6
references.take: Circle's member-invite screen offers manual, CSV and link entry, plus an explicit 'Send invites' versus 'Add without notification' choice. It shows notification intent, not email delivery or finished course enrollment.

references.title: A skip-email option that fails the invite
references.question: Q6
references.take: On Cloudflare's workspace invite, selecting 'Skip confirmation email' produces an Enterprise-only error and the invitation fails. The screen makes the failed action visible; it does not show a course enrollment outcome.

references.title: Explain enrollment emails before purchase
references.question: Q6
references.take: Gusto's pre-purchase 'What happens next' section says Gusto will email course information and a link, learners complete the course in Gusto, and the admin tracks progress. This describes future behavior, not an email already sent or received.
